theme: 3 terms on copying objects: a copy that shares the objects inside, a copy that duplicates them too, and the Foundation protocol a class adopts to copy itself

terms.definition: A copy that duplicates only the outer value, so the class instances inside are still shared with the original.
terms.example: Copying the cart is only a Shallow Copy, the items are still the same objects.
terms.code:
class Box { var n = 1 }
let a = [Box()]
let b = a // copies the references
b[0].n = 9
print(a[0].n)

terms.definition: A copy that also duplicates every object inside, so changing the copy never touches the original.
terms.example: Make a Deep Copy before editing, or the undo history changes too.

terms.definition: A Foundation protocol a class adopts to say how a new, separate copy of it is made in `copy(with:)`.
terms.example: Our `Document` class adopts NSCopying, so every copy is a separate instance.

quizzes.question: Which Foundation protocol lets a class decide how a separate copy of it is made?
In this code, what kind of copy is `b`, since changing it also changes `a`?
quizzes.code:
class Box { var n = 1 }
let a = [Box()]
let b = a
b[0].n = 9

quizzes.question: What do you call a copy that also duplicates every object inside, so nothing is shared?

video.description:
Learn to explain copying objects in Swift: Shallow Copy, Deep Copy & NSCopying, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Shallow Copy - A copy that duplicates only the outer value, so the class instances inside are still shared with the original.
Deep Copy - A copy that also duplicates every object inside, so changing the copy never touches the original.
NSCopying - A Foundation protocol a class adopts to say how a new, separate copy of it is made in `copy(with:)`.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift Shallow Copy, Deep Copy & NSCopying | Day 75
landscape.description:
Explain Shallow Copy, Deep Copy & NSCopying in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
얕은 복사, 깊은 복사, NSCopying 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Shallow Copy - A copy that duplicates only the outer value, so the class instances inside are still shared with the original.
한국어: 얕은 복사: 바깥 값만 복제해서 안에 든 클래스 인스턴스는 원본과 계속 공유하는 복사

Deep Copy - A copy that also duplicates every object inside, so changing the copy never touches the original.
한국어: 깊은 복사: 안에 든 객체까지 모두 복제해서 복사본을 바꿔도 원본에는 영향이 없는 복사

NSCopying - A Foundation protocol a class adopts to say how a new, separate copy of it is made in `copy(with:)`.
한국어: NSCopying: 클래스가 `copy(with:)`에서 자신의 새롭고 독립된 복사본을 만드는 방법을 정하기 위해 채택하는 Foundation 프로토콜

In this video, Mina and Jake duplicate a playlist, watch the original change too and pick a way to really copy the songs, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.
Mina와 Jake의 채팅 스타일 대화와 화면 속 Swift 코드로 배워요.

landscape.hook: I edited the copy and the original changed. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Why did mine change?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I renamed a song in `dupe`, and `mine` changed too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: `Playlist` is a struct, but `Song` is a class. That's a Shallow Copy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wait, didn't copying the struct copy everything?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It copied the array, but the array holds references to the same songs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So both playlists point at one `Song`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. A Shallow Copy shares the objects inside.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I need a Deep Copy, with new `Song` objects.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. Make `Song` adopt NSCopying and copy each song.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why not just change `Song` to a struct?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That works too. If `Song` must stay a class, use NSCopying.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. NSCopying gives each song a twin, and `dupe` becomes a Deep Copy.
A struct full of classes only gives you a Shallow Copy.
